correctness.rationale: PASS: For r>=3 complete multipartite, D is total outer-independent dominating iff Y=V\D is contained in one part: independence gives necessity, and at least r−1>=2 fully selected other parts ensure sufficiency for total domination. Taking y,z in different parts and the partition (V\{y,z},{y},{z}) yields 3 non-TOIDS blocks with each a coalition partner. For any supposed >=4-block partition take coalition A,B; all other blocks lie in the one part P containing V\(A∪B). A remaining C cannot partner A (or B), because B and an additional remaining block lie in the complement of A∪C, forcing B⊆P and then A itself TOIDS. Nor can two remaining blocks C,E⊆P be total dominating (all vertices inside P have no neighbor in C∪E), contradiction. Hence at most 3. Independently enumerated all set partitions and definition-level predicates for K(1,1,2), K(1,2,2), K(2,2,2), K(1,1,1,3): maxima 3. All-part-size conclusion rests on symbolic proof. Complete graphs excluded as prior-covered and r=2 separate.
